items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: the time when Maude was at the table

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah. And Bunk was very pleased with Don. He used to get up and walk around and stand beside the piano and play a solo, which before that he had never made very much of a point of playing solos, I don't think. I mean, he had certain solos he'd do in certain numbers, but he'd just stand up and do them. He really tried to do a little more with setting off his solos as apart from the ensembles. When Don was with the band, he'd go over and stand next to the piano and do a real solo type solo and very pretty…

That second engagement, if I remember rightly, was the only one when Maude was up there, too. There was something you were telling the other night, the time when Maude was at the table. I forget what the story is now, but you were there once when she was there in New York, too.

Yeah, well, I was telling a couple stories the other night, happening to be at the Stuyvesant when there was conflict in the band, when Bunk was having trouble with a drummer. And I guess I get Bunk actually had trouble with both drummers, Baby and Steel.
